name: earnings_surprise_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (PEAD) is one of the most robust anomalies in finance. In Indian markets, earnings are typically announced after market hours (16:00-20:00 IST) or before market open. Stocks that gap >2% at open on result days exhibit intraday momentum continuation in the gap direction for the first 60-90 minutes, driven by: (1) retail traders who read the headline but take 30+ minutes to act, (2) mutual fund NAV-driven flows that execute throughout the day, (3) analyst upgrades/downgrades that trickle in during the session, amplifying the initial move. The intraday drift is 30-50% of the gap magnitude on average. The inefficiency persists because many traders fade gaps (expecting reversion) when the correct action on earnings gaps is to follow the gap direction.
universe: NIFTY 200 constituents (only on their result days)
stock_filter: Stock must have announced earnings in the last 18 hours, ADV > ₹15 crore
session: 09:15-12:00 IST (first 2.75 hours only — drift fades after noon)

conditions: close_5min > open_today (gap not fading in first 5 minutes)
long.confirmation: close at 09:20 > high of 09:15-09:20 range (breakout above opening range)

conditions: close_5min < open_today (gap not bouncing in first 5 minutes)

exit.target: 50% of gap magnitude as continuation target (e.g., gap=3%, target=1.5% further)
exit.stop_loss: gap fills 50% (e.g., gap=3%, stop if retraces 1.5%)
exit.trailing_stop: 20 bps trailing after 30 bps of continuation achieved
exit.time_stop: exit by 12:00 IST regardless (drift exhausts by midday)
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 12:00 IST (not 15:29 — drift is a morning phenomenon)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L, reduce to ₹50K for stocks with ADV < ₹30 crore

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (earnings drift works across vol regimes)
filters.volume_filter: volume_surge > 2.0 on opening bars (must be heavily traded result day)
filters.trend_filter: prefer gap direction aligned with NIFTY 50 direction (tailwind)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 15 bps (spreads widen on result day but must be tradeable)
filters.event_filter: only trade on result day, not day after (PEAD at daily level is different)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — PEAD is one of the most persistent anomalies in finance, documented since Ball & Brown (1968). In India, the anomaly is still strong because retail gap-faders provide liquidity for drift traders.

weaknesses: Earnings surprise data (consensus estimates) is not freely available real-time. Bloomberg/Refinitiv subscriptions cost ₹10L+/year, creating a data barrier.
Gap direction and earnings quality may disagree — a positive gap on low-quality earnings (one-time gains) will revert, not drift. Qualitative filtering is needed but hard to automate.
The strategy generates trades only during result season (~8 weeks/year across 4 quarters), leaving it idle for ~70% of trading days.
prior_art: Ball & Brown (1968) original PEAD discovery. Bernard & Thomas (1989, 1990) confirm persistence. In India, Dutta & Girish (2013) study PEAD in BSE stocks. DellaVigna & Pollet (2009) show PEAD is stronger when investor attention is low (Friday announcements).
notes: Consider using option IV crush as a confirming signal — if IV drops significantly on result day open, it means the move is in line with expected; if IV stays elevated, the market expects more movement. The opening range breakout (09:15-09:20) filter is critical to avoid fading into gap-fill traps.
